You are a supply-chain anomaly analyst. You receive one event feed as a
JSON object and must return a single JSON assessment object and nothing else.

Output schema (all fields required):
{
  "is_anomaly": true | false,
  "anomaly_class": "demand_spike" | "demand_collapse" | "supplier_shipment_delay" |
                   "port_logistics_congestion" | "weather_disruption" | "quality_hold" |
                   "labor_strike" | "freight_inflation" | "inventory_obsolescence" |
                   "warehouse_capacity_breach" | "none",
  "severity": <integer 1 (trivial) to 5 (critical)>,
  "root_cause": "<2-4 sentences grounded only in the feed>",
  "evidence_fields": ["<input field names that justify the class>"],
  "corrective_actions": ["<3-5 concrete, actionable steps>"],
  "confidence": <number between 0 and 1>
}

Rules:
- Use anomaly_class "none" with is_anomaly false for normal feeds.
- Cite only input field names that exist in the feed.
- Never mention events that the feed does not contain.
- Severity guide: 1 trivial, 2 minor, 3 material, 4 severe, 5 critical.

Return ONLY the JSON object.

{"inventory_days_on_hand":31.0,"labor_document_note":"none","notes":"Inbound apparel shipments arrived on schedule and a minor 3% forecast miss was absorbed by existing safety stock with no operational impact.","on_time_delivery_pct":96.4,"order_volume_vs_forecast_pct":-3.0,"port_congestion_index":27.0,"product_category":"apparel","region":"Europe","supplier_status":"normal","transit_days_normal":12.0,"transit_days_observed":12.0,"unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct":0.8,"weather_event":"none"}

{"anomaly_class":"none","confidence":0.95,"corrective_actions":["No intervention required; continue the standard daily monitoring cadence.","Fold the latest sell-through data into the next forecast cycle to keep forecast error within +/-5%.","Maintain the current replenishment schedule and safety-stock levels.","Log the benign variance in the weekly S&OP review for trend tracking only."],"evidence_fields":["order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","inventory_days_on_hand","on_time_delivery_pct","transit_days_observed","port_congestion_index"],"is_anomaly":false,"root_cause":"Order volume came in 3% below forecast, which is within normal forecast tolerance for the apparel category and was fully absorbed by the 31 days of inventory on hand. Supplier status is normal, on-time delivery is at 96.4%, and observed transit matches the normal 12 days with low port congestion at 27. No weather events or labor notes are present, and unit costs are essentially flat versus last quarter, so all operational metrics sit within their normal ranges.","severity":1}

{"inventory_days_on_hand":31.0,"labor_document_note":"none","notes":"Retailer replenishment orders fell far below forecast through the week while inbound receipts continued on schedule, pushing perishable stock coverage well above the usual 12-15 day target.","on_time_delivery_pct":98.4,"order_volume_vs_forecast_pct":-46.0,"port_congestion_index":21.0,"product_category":"food_and_beverage","region":"Europe","supplier_status":"normal","transit_days_normal":4.0,"transit_days_observed":4.0,"unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct":-2.1,"weather_event":"none"}

{"anomaly_class":"demand_collapse","confidence":0.92,"corrective_actions":["Immediately cut or pause inbound purchase orders and reschedule supplier deliveries to match actual sell-through rather than the stale forecast.","Trigger an urgent demand re-forecast with the commercial team and review retailer order patterns and the promotional calendar to locate the drop.","Enforce strict FIFO rotation and prioritize outbound allocation of the oldest perishable stock to limit shelf-life expiry risk.","Redistribute excess inventory to other European DCs or secondary/discount channels to relieve storage pressure and avoid write-offs.","Track margin impact given the -2.1% unit-cost move and evaluate pricing or trade-spend adjustments to stimulate demand."],"evidence_fields":["order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","inventory_days_on_hand","on_time_delivery_pct","unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"Outbound order volume collapsed to 46% below forecast while supplier status, transit times, port congestion, and on-time delivery all remained at normal levels, indicating a demand-side contraction rather than any supply disruption. Because inbound receipts continued at forecast-based schedules, inventory coverage swelled to 31 days on hand, far above typical levels for perishable food and beverage SKUs. The mild unit-cost decline and absence of weather, labor, or logistics signals further confirm weak downstream demand as the sole driver.","severity":4}

{"anomaly_class":"demand_spike","confidence":0.92,"corrective_actions":["Expedite replenishment purchase orders for the affected beverage SKUs to rebuild days on hand above 10.","Update the demand forecast to reflect the promotional uplift and re-run weekly netting for the region.","Temporarily prioritize allocation of constrained SKUs to highest-velocity distribution centers.","Add a short-term picking/outbound shift to protect on-time delivery while volume remains elevated.","Monitor daily sell-through and order intake to distinguish a sustained uplift from a short promotional pulse."],"evidence_fields":["order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","inventory_days_on_hand","on_time_delivery_pct","notes"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"Order volume is running 27% above forecast, driven by sustained consumer demand rather than any supply-side disruption. Inventory cover has compressed to 6.5 days on hand, and on-time delivery slipped modestly to 94.8% as picking and outbound capacity absorb the extra volume. Supplier, transit, and port conditions remain normal, confirming this is a demand-side event.","severity":2}

{"inventory_days_on_hand":24.0,"labor_document_note":"none","notes":"Inbound freight rates on our Midwest outbound lanes have risen steadily this quarter, adding about 16% to landed unit cost while suppliers and labor remain unaffected.","on_time_delivery_pct":93.0,"order_volume_vs_forecast_pct":102.0,"port_congestion_index":58.0,"product_category":"food_and_beverage","region":"North America","supplier_status":"normal","transit_days_normal":5.0,"transit_days_observed":6.0,"unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct":16.0,"weather_event":"none"}

{"anomaly_class":"freight_inflation","confidence":0.88,"corrective_actions":["Rebid the affected North America lanes and renegotiate carrier contracts with volume commitments to cap surcharges","Shift a portion of volume from expedited truckload to intermodal rail where transit slack allows","Negotiate fixed fuel-surcharge tables or fuel hedges with primary carriers for the next two quarters","Review customer pricing and margin thresholds to recover part of the 16% landed-cost increase","Track lane-level freight cost per pallet weekly with an escalation trigger if unit cost rises beyond 20%"],"evidence_fields":["unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct","transit_days_normal","transit_days_observed","port_congestion_index","on_time_delivery_pct"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"Landed unit cost is up 16% versus last quarter while demand (102% of forecast), supplier status, inventory cover, and labor conditions are all normal, isolating the cost increase to transportation. Mildly longer transit (6 observed vs 5 normal days) and an elevated port congestion index of 58 on North America lanes are consistent with carriers adding congestion and fuel surcharges. On-time delivery has slipped modestly to 93%, reflecting the same slower, costlier freight environment rather than any supply or demand disruption.","severity":2}

{"anomaly_class":"none","confidence":0.95,"corrective_actions":["Continue the standard replenishment cadence to maintain ~24 days of inventory coverage through the holiday period.","Monitor daily order volume against forecast to catch any shift from benign seasonal uplift into a true demand spike.","Keep tracking transit days and the port congestion index for early warning of inbound delays.","Maintain current safety stock levels and supplier lead-time assumptions; no escalation required.","Review supplier status and on-time delivery at the next weekly cycle to confirm continued normal performance."],"evidence_fields":["order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","inventory_days_on_hand","on_time_delivery_pct","supplier_status","transit_days_observed","port_congestion_index","unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct"],"is_anomaly":false,"root_cause":"Order volume is modestly above forecast, consistent with routine seasonal holiday demand, and is being absorbed without strain: inventory coverage is healthy at 24 days and supplier status is normal. On-time delivery remains high at 96.5% with observed transit times essentially matching the normal baseline, and the port congestion index is low. Unit cost change is within routine quarterly variation, and no weather or labor events are reported, so all operational metrics sit within their normal ranges.","severity":1}

{"anomaly_class":"inventory_obsolescence","confidence":0.92,"corrective_actions":["Freeze all replenishment purchase orders for the aged winter knitwear SKUs immediately","Launch a clearance program: outlet channel, e-commerce flash sale, and B2B jobber lots to move aged stock","Apply a progressive markdown ladder and record the required inventory write-down with finance","Flag all SKUs above 180 days on hand for a weekly obsolescence review with an aging report by season","Rebalance the next season's buy plan in S&OP against the updated demand forecast to prevent a repeat overbuy"],"evidence_fields":["inventory_days_on_hand","order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct","notes"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"Inventory days on hand has ballooned to 240 days while order volume runs 45% below forecast, indicating prior-season apparel stock is not selling through and is aging into obsolescence. {"inventory_days_on_hand":42.0,"labor_document_note":"Dockworker union strike at primary Asia-Pacific transshipment port now in day 6; container handling running at ~35% of normal throughput with no confirmed resolution date","notes":"Outbound container bookings are queuing at the strike-affected terminal while inbound components sit on anchored vessels, pushing finished-goods inventory well above target.","on_time_delivery_pct":57.0,"order_volume_vs_forecast_pct":103.0,"port_congestion_index":79.0,"product_category":"electronics","region":"Asia-Pacific","supplier_status":"delayed","transit_days_normal":12.0,"transit_days_observed":21.0,"unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct":9.0,"weather_event":"none"}

{"anomaly_class":"labor_strike","confidence":0.94,"corrective_actions":["Reroute pending inbound and outbound containers to secondary regional ports not affected by the strike, accepting longer inland drayage","Air-freight only the highest-margin or customer-critical electronics SKUs to protect key orders","Proactively notify affected customers of revised delivery dates and offer substitution options from other fulfillment nodes","Rebalance safety stock by pulling inventory from unaffected regional warehouses to cover near-term orders","Track union negotiation status daily and pre-book post-strike vessel capacity to clear the backlog quickly"],"evidence_fields":["labor_document_note","port_congestion_index","transit_days_observed","transit_days_normal","on_time_delivery_pct","inventory_days_on_hand","unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct","supplier_status"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"The feed explicitly reports a day-6 dockworker strike at the primary Asia-Pacific transshipment port, with container handling down to ~35% of normal throughput. This labor action is the proximate cause of the elevated port congestion index (79) and the transit stretch from 12 to 21 observed days. Stalled vessel turnarounds and blocked outbound bookings explain the collapse in on-time delivery to 57% and the buildup of inventory to 42 days on hand, while demurrage and expedite premiums account for the 9% unit cost increase. Demand itself remains near forecast at 103%, confirming a logistics-side disruption rather than a demand problem.","severity":4}
